analysis.summary: NNTailor drives DBMS fuzzing with a neural network: a model trained on SQL learns how to mutate queries so they stay syntactically and semantically valid, instead of relying on hand-written templates. On the latest PostgreSQL and SQLite it reports 35% higher line coverage than SQLsmith and 10% higher than SQLancer, along with better validity of the generated queries.
analysis.narrative: SQLancer is one of NNTailor's two baselines, compared on code coverage and on the syntactic and semantic correctness of generated queries. The paper attributes SQLancer's coverage ceiling to template reliance -- predefined rules achieve considerable coverage but bound how much of the code space can be explored -- while acknowledging the other side of that trade: because SQLancer's oracles require expressions built to predefined semantic rules, it achieves high semantic correctness on SQLite. The comparison is reported as mixed rather than one-sided, with the paper noting that the two tools have their own advantages on different systems.

uses_infrastructure.reasoning: SQLancer is run as a baseline; NNTailor's generation is driven by a neural network model of its own.

extends_technique.reasoning: No SQLancer oracle is extended. NNTailor changes how queries are produced, not what makes a result wrong.
